section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the Yalkut's story of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and Rabbi Yehoshua, explaining that the "other atonement" of gemilus chassadim refers specifically to prayer (iyn tephilah), which was instituted in exile and is a form of drawing down from Above, unlike individual sacrifices which are an elevation.
section.t: Now, it is brought in the Yalkut
on the verse "For I desire kindness and not sacrifice,"
Once, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was walking in Yerushalayim,
and Rabbi Yehoshua was walking after him.
He saw the Beis HaMikdash, that it was destroyed.
He said,
"Woe to us over the House that is destroyed, the place where our iniquities were atoned!"
He [Rabbi Yehoshua] said to him,
"My son, do not be distressed,
for we have another atonement that is like it.
And which is it?
It is gemilus chassadim [acts of lovingkindness]."
Therefore it says, "For I desire kindness and not sacrifice."
And it says,
"I said: The world is built with kindness."
And it is precise in the discourses,
[that] gemilus chassadim also existed during the time when the Beis HaMikdash was standing,
and from the wording "we have another atonement" it implies that this atonement was innovated during the time of exile.
And it is explained there,
based on what is brought in the Gemara:
Rabbi Yochanan said,
"Six things a person eats their fruits in this world, and the principal remains for him in the World to Come"
(and iyun tephilah [meditative prayer] is among the six things).
And the Gemara asks,
"But we learned in a Mishnah
'These are the things that a person does and eats their fruits in this world, etc.' and it lists only three things,"
and it answers,
"These [three] are also included in those [six]."
And Rashi explained,
that iyun tephilah is included in gemilus chassadim, as it is written,
"He who is kind to his own soul is a man of kindness"
[And "nefesh" [soul] refers to prayer, as it is written regarding Chanah,
"And I poured out my soul before Hashem"].
And it is explained in the discourses,
that what Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said, "we have another atonement... gemilus chassadim,"
his intention is iyun tephilah, which is included in gemilus chassadim
[for the essence of prayer
(the three prayers each day and the text of the prayer)
was instituted during the time of exile].
And although prayers are in place of sacrifices, and sacrifices are an elevation from below to Above,
it is explained in the discourses,
that "prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily and additional offerings,"
and the daily and additional offerings,
communal sacrifices,
are a level of drawing down.
As it is brought in the Midrash,
that the reason Yisrael is called by the name "My friend"
is because they would offer two daily offerings upon the altar,
and through this they are "My friend,"
"My sustainer" —
Yisrael sustain their Father in Heaven,
in that they draw down Ein Sof into the Sefiros.
And what is written "For I desire kindness and not sacrifice" refers to individual sacrifices,
which are a level of elevation,
but communal sacrifices,
the daily and additional offerings,
are a level of drawing down.
And as the Shach wrote in his commentary on the Torah
on the verse,
"Besides the burnt offering of the morning,"
that "besides" is an acronym for
"One who lends"
"to a poor person"
"at the time of"
"his distress,"
and the explanation of "Besides the burnt offering of the morning" is,
that one who lends to a poor person at the time of his distress is like the burnt offering of the morning,
the continual offering,
which is a drawing down from Above to below.
And from this, that prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings,
it is understood
that prayers are a drawing down from Above to below.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the gemilus chassadim of prayer, instituted after the destruction, has an advantage over simple gemilus chassadim, as prayer involves both an elevation (pouring out the soul) and a drawing down, with two interpretations of "gomel nafsho" relating to the Divine and animal souls.
section.t: Now, from the fact that gemilus chassadim
(in its simple sense)
also existed during the time of the Beis HaMikdash,
whereas the gemilus chassadim of prayer
("He who is kind to his own soul is a man of kindness")
was instituted specifically after the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash,
in order that there should also now be the atonement similar to the atonement that was through the Beis HaMikdash,
"the place where our iniquities were atoned,"
it is understood
that there is an advantage in the atonement effected through the gemilus chassadim of prayer over the atonement through gemilus chassadim in its simple sense.
And the concept is,
that prayer
(in general)
is an elevation from below to Above,
as is also understood from what is written, "And I poured out my soul before Hashem"
[for from this verse they bring a proof that prayer is a drawing down],
for the pouring out of the soul is an elevation,
except that the request of this elevation is that there should be a drawing down below.
[And to add,
it is explained in the discourses,
that regarding "He who is kind to his own soul is a man of kindness,"
there are two explanations.
"Gomel" from the term of weaning/separating
(like "And the child grew and was weaned"),
and "gomel" from the term of bestowing influence
(like gemilus chassadim).
"Gomel nafsho" from the term of bestowing influence is in the service of prayer from the side of the Nefesh HaElokis,
where the elevation
(pouring out of the soul)
is for the sake of the drawing down.
And "gomel nafsho" from the term of weaning/separating is in the offering up of the Nefesh HaBahamis in prayer,
to separate and depart from worldly matters and to be in a state of nullification,
[which is] elevation.
And in the service from the side of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
the elevation is not for the sake of a drawing down, but rather this itself is its request.
And it can be said,
that this [fact] that the prayer of the Nefesh HaElokis is called by the name "gomel nafsho,"
where "gomel" is also a term of weaning/separating,
indicates,
that also in the prayer of the Nefesh HaElokis there is an elevation analogous to the elevation of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
[in that] its request is [also] elevation].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains two aspects of forgiveness and atonement: one through drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is separate from will and nullifies defects, and another through drawing from the Essence as the Master of Will, which brings a new will that reconciles Him.
section.t: Now, it is known that in forgiveness and atonement there are two concepts.
Through the drawing down from the Essence of Ein Sof, the Master of Will Who is not compelled in the will,
the sins and blemishes are nullified.
And there is another concept in forgiveness and atonement,
that through the drawing down from the Essence of Ein Sof, the Master of Will,
a new will is drawn down
(which is above the will that was removed through the sin),
and through this, He becomes appeased before Him, blessed be He, as before the sin.
And the difference between these two concepts is,
that this [aspect] that through the drawing down from the Essence of Ein Sof the blemishes are nullified is because He is not compelled in the will,
[He is] separate from the will,
and this [aspect] that a new will is drawn from Him is
(not because He is separate from the will,
but rather, on the contrary)
because He is the Master of Will.
For in the level of will,
there is limitation in the manner of its drawing down,
and when one does the opposite of the will, it departs.
But the Master of Will,
is not limited in the manner of the drawing down,
and therefore, even after they have done the opposite of the will, through which the will departed,
it is possible for a new will to be drawn from Him.
